# Wiki Surface Cell Grammars

The grammars a `ui-surface` page's cells take where they name where an action leads, which flow steps happen on a surface and what kind an action is, and how a platform copy of a bullet reads. `wiki-cell-grammars` holds how a template declares a grammar, and the rules every grammar shares.

**See also:** `wiki-authoring-spec` — for the readability rules and the list of every author-facing lookup.
**See also:** `wiki-cell-grammars` — for the `Cells:` label, pending cells and what stays judgment.
**See also:** `wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars` — for the bullets that place a surface, and the heading kind.

## Surface cell grammars

- **`surface-link`** — where an action leads when it succeeds: `—` when the user stays, or one
  or more destinations separated by `;`. A destination is a target, then an optional platform tag
  `(<platform>)` from the surface's own platforms, then an optional scope
  `in [[design:information-architecture/<page>]]`, then an optional `when <condition>`, which stays
  prose. The targets:
  - `[[design:surfaces/<page-path>#<surface-anchor>]]` — a named surface, on this page or another,
    always with the `design:` prefix and the anchor. The anchor is the slug of the surface's whole
    heading, kind included (`wiki-conventions` §Cross-reference protocol), so a named surface
    whose heading slugs the same as an earlier heading on the page is an error;
  - `[[design:components/<path>]]` — a dialog or other reused component; a variant it opens in
    stays in `Consequence` prose;
  - `back` — wherever the user came from;
  - `external` — a step out of the product;
  - `Pending: <surface name>` — a surface not specified yet, bound as a pending cell (`wiki-cell-grammars` §Cell grammars).

  A scoped destination counts only where its scope holds (the scope bullet below). Each of
  several destinations carries a tag, a scope or a condition, so a reader can tell which applies.
  A failure stays on the surface, as `Consequence`'s error state says, so `Leads to` names only
  where success goes. A link whose page does not exist, or whose anchor matches no heading, is
  `/wiki-lint`'s error; the audit errors on a surface link to a page that is not a `ui-surface`,
  a component link to a page that is not a `ui-component`, an anchor naming a heading that is not
  a named surface, a tag outside the surface's own platforms (the page's `platforms:`, narrowed
  by the surface's Platforms bullet), and a bad scope (`surface-link/wrong-scope`).
- **A scope** — `in [[design:information-architecture/<page>]]` at the end of an entry: a Leads
  to destination, a Shown in entry or an Opened from entry
  (`wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars`). A scoped entry counts only in an application whose
  composed sitemap includes the scope page: the application's own page, or a part or skeleton it
  includes. That holds in placement and in the journey walk alike. Each grammar errors on a scope
  that is no `design:` link to an `information-architecture` page, under its own `wrong-scope`
  code; a scope naming no page is `/wiki-lint`'s error.
- **`flow-steps`** — the steps of the page's flows that happen on the surface: `None.` when no
  step lands there, or one group per flow separated by `;`, each the flow's
  `[[product:flows/<module>/<flow-slug>]]` link and its step ids separated by `,`:
  `[[product:flows/billing/pay-invoice]] S1, S2, E1`. An id is the flow's own — `S`, `A`, `E` or
  `T` and its number — and a flow specializing a shared base is cited by its own ids, the base only
  where `flows:` lists it too. A step the flow marks as happening on no product surface
  (`**S4 (external) — …**`, `system` or `agent` likewise) may be named too, meaning the surface
  shows that step's progress or outcome. The audit errors on a value in none of these forms, a
  link to a page that is not a `task-flow`, a flow the page's `flows:` does not list, an id the
  flow does not define, and an id carrying the ` (external)` marker (`S4 (external)`), reported as
  `flow-steps/surface-marker`: the flow's label carries the marker, `**S4 (external) — …**`. On a
  page where any surface carries the bullet, it also errors on a flow `flows:` lists that no
  surface names a step of.
  `flow-step-coverage` asks a surface placement of unmarked steps only: an unmarked step of a
  listed flow that no surface of any page listing the flow places is a warning rather than an
  error, because the surface that places it may still be in progress on another page. To clear
  it, place the step under the `Flow steps` of the surface where it happens, adding the flow to
  that page's `flows:` if it does not list it, or mark the step on the flow's label. A page
  stamped below the template version that added `Flow steps` gets no coverage warning.
- **`Kind`** — an `Actions` row's kind, a `one-of` value defined by the action's effect:
  `primary` is the surface's main commitment; `secondary` is a change that is not the main task
  and stays on the surface (record a pick, retry, start afresh, cancel or discard an edit);
  `destructive` removes or cannot be undone; `nav` moves to another place and changes nothing;
  `view` changes what the surface shows and records nothing (search, filter, sort, clear a
  search). A named surface holds at most one `primary`, counted across the shared Actions table
  and any one platform copy. A `view` action leads to `—`; a `nav` action does not.
  `surface-action-kinds` checks these, an error.
- **A platform copy** — a copy of a block bullet such as `**Actions (web)**` serves one view of
  the surface, and its qualifier is one of the surface's own platforms
  (`wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars` § Surface placement cell grammars); a region with
  content of its own is a named surface of its own. A copy of Container, Node, Shown in or Opened
  from overrides the shared value for its platform. Platforms and Journey stages take no copy. A copy of any other
  bullet adds to the shared bullet. `bullet-qualifier` checks the qualifier and the refusal, an
  error; it errors on a copy qualified by a platform the surface leaves out.
